headline: Revenue and profit climb sharply; forward guidance initiated
summary_short: Tapestry reported EPS of $1.32 for its fiscal fourth quarter (ended June 27, 2026), swinging from a $2.49 per-share loss in the year-ago quarter as net sales rose 9% to $1.88 billion.
summary_long: Net sales rose 9% reported (12% pro forma, ex-Stuart Weitzman) to $1.88 billion, led by 15% Coach growth that offset a 7% decline at Kate Spade. Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.32 rose 28% year-over-year, aided by 25% non-GAAP operating-income growth and a $98.3 million IEEPA tariff refund. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.68 versus a $(2.49) loss a year earlier, when an $854.8 million Kate Spade impairment weighed on results. Cash and short-term investments totaled $1.15 billion against $2.38 billion of total debt. The company repurchased $1.35 billion of stock and raised its dividend 16% to an annualized $1.85 per share. Tapestry initiated fiscal 2027 guidance: mid-single-digit revenue growth to $8.4-$8.5 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $7.80-$7.90.
confidence_notes: Reported figures are for Tapestry's fiscal fourth quarter (ended June 27, 2026); our shard labels this event 'FY2026 Q2' due to a fiscal-calendar period-mapping mismatch — a labeling artifact, not a data error (see CLAUDE.md's fiscal-offset-issuer note; TPR is not on the documented list but shows the same failure class). The prior-year GAAP EPS comparison (-$2.49) includes an $854.8 million Kate Spade brand/goodwill impairment; Non-GAAP EPS excludes it and rose 28% y/y per the company's own reconciliation. The FY2027 outlook is presented on a non-GAAP basis without a full GAAP reconciliation because certain reconciling items are not yet estimable.

Non-GAAP diluted EPS grew on 25% non-GAAP operating-income growth and a $98.3M IEEPA tariff refund, partly offset by organizational-efficiency and distribution-network-optimization costs.
Not explicitly attributed by the release; the decline is consistent with the $1.35B of share buybacks and $326M of dividends the company disclosed returning to shareholders in fiscal 2026.
